REGENT OF GORONTALO

GORONTALO PROVINCE

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GORONTALO REGENCY

NUMBER 9 OF 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE  BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

heading: REGENT OF GORONTALO,
translated_text:
REGENT OF GORONTALO,

Considering:
a. that Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantee the right of every citizen to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence:

b. that all forms of acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination,

c. that women's empowerment and child protection are concurrent governmental affairs delegated to the regions to become the basis for implementing regional autonomy and become mandatory governmental affairs not related to basic services as referred to in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government,

d. that in order to provide regulatory strengthening, direction, and foundation in the protection of women and children victims of violence, regulation is needed related to the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence,

In view of: that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, letter c, and letter d, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Against Acts of Violence,

WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

BABI

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs — which are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
0. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or ind
11. 12. 13. 14, Region.

Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.

Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.

Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

Safe House is a shelter for victims, during

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting

19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Protection of Victims is based on:

a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims,

b. justice and gender equality,

Cc. non-discrimination:

d. the best interests of victims, dan

e. empowerment.

heading: Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

Protection of Victims aims to:

a. prevent violence against women and children,

b. provide services to Victims, dan

c. empower women victims of violence.

heading: Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

The scope of this Regional Regulation includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the Region.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

FORMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 5

Forms of violence include:

a. physical violence,

b. psychological violence,

Cc. sexual violence,

d. neglect,

e. exploitation, and/or 1 other violence.

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a results in injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is caused by:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse,

Cc. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, and/or

d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

Neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is caused by:

a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care,

b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should be carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care,

Cc. acts of neglecting people within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person, dan/atau,

d. -.8- acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial, dan /atau any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:

a. threats of violence which include any unlawful act in the form of words, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict the fundamental freedom of a person, dan coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

heading: CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 12

Every Victim has the right to:
a. have their dignity and worth as a human being respected;
b. restoration of health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim;

and to determine their own decisions, obtain information, confidentiality of their identity, compensation, social rehabilitation, complaint handling, obtain facilitation in the judicial process, and/or assistance.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

Child victims of violence, in addition to obtaining the rights as referred to in Article 12, also obtain special rights, which consist of:
a. respect for survival, growth and development, basic services, equal protection, freedom from various stigma, and/or obtaining freedom.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Part One

Regional Government

heading: Article 14
Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to:
a. supervise the implementation of services to victims, with minimum service standards; and
b. provide a budget for victim protection through the APBD and/or other lawful Regional financial sources.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community and Family

heading: Article 16
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

P2TP2A

Article 17

1. P2TP2A is established by the Regional Government and/or community institutions.
2. The organizational structure of P2TP2A established by the regional government as referred to in paragraph (1) is established according to needs.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The Gorontalo Regency Government provides a Safe House as a form of service and protection for victims of violence through P2TP2A.
2. The safe house referred to in paragraph (1) is equipped with facilities and infrastructure.

heading: Article 19
Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. P2TP2A established by the Regional Government must have at least three counselors.
2. Counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. counselor in the field of law;
b. counselor in the field of health; and
c. counselor in the field of psychology.
d. counselor in other fields.
3. The implementation of counseling carried out by counselors may be implemented in a networked manner as follows:
a. counseling in the field of law by involving the Police, Prosecutor's Office, District Court, Religious Court, Regional Government Legal Division, Legal Advocacy Institutions, and community organizations;
b. counseling in the field of health by involving the Health Office, Regional General Hospital, and other health services;
c. counseling in the field of psychology by involving psychological companions and/or psychologists.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Prevention

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. Efforts to prevent violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by regional apparatus that administer government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:
a. forming a work network in efforts to prevent violence;
b. the work network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1. task force on violence against women and children,
2. Bele lomongoditi moli,
3. Children's Forum,
4. Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5. Suami sayang istri;
c. forming a violence prevention system;
d. conducting socialization about laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence; and
e. providing critical education about the rights of women and children for the community.
3. The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the duties of the work network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

In addition to the Regional Government, prevention efforts as referred to in Article 21 paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. family and/or closest relatives,
b. community,
c. educational institutions, and Non-Governmental Organizations.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Services

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

The implementation of services to victims is carried out in an integrated manner by P2TP2A.

P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) may:
2. receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

The implementation of services to victims is carried out with:
a. speed,
b. safety and comfort,
c. a sense of empathy,
d. non-discrimination,

and is easy to access, free of charge, and confidentiality is guaranteed.

heading: Article 25
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

Services as referred to in Article 25 letter a include:
a. identification or initial recording of victims; and
b. consent for action to be taken.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

Assistance services as referred to in Article 25 letter b include:
a. accompanying victims during the examination and health recovery process,
b. accompanying victims during the medicolegal process,
c. accompanying victims during the examination process at the Police, Prosecutor's Office and court,
d. monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the Police, Prosecutor's Office and Court,
e. maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including reporting by mass media,
f. coordinating with other companions, and
g. providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Health services as referred to in Article 25 letter c include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 25 letter d are services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. Legal services as referred to in Article 25 letter e are intended to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
2. Legal services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. providing legal consultation which includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process,
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced,
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 25 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. Regency/City Governments within one Provincial area,
b. related government and non-government agencies and institutions.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Empowerment

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

Empowerment of women victims of violence includes:

a. job training,

b. productive economic enterprises and/or joint business groups, and

c. capital assistance.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

Job training as referred to in Article 32 letter a includes:

a. skills training,

b. field work practice, and

c. apprenticeship.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

Productive economic enterprises and/or joint business groups as referred to in Article 32 letter b include:

a. entrepreneurial skills training,

b. facilitation of joint business group formation, and

c. business implementation assistance.

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

Capital assistance as referred to in Article 32 letter c includes:

a. work facilities and infrastructure assistance, and

b. working capital assistance facilitation.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Fulfillment of the Rights of Child Victims of Violence

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. The Regional Government, P2TP2A, and the community are obliged to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence.
2. Forms of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include fulfillment of children's basic rights according to their needs.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Coordination of Victim Protection

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. In efforts to protect and provide service handling for victims, the Regional Government.
2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. Regional FPKK,
b. Sub-district FPKK, and
c. Urban Village/Village FPKK.
3. Establishment of Regional FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall be stipulated by Regent's decree.
4. Establishment of Sub-district FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b shall be stipulated by Sub-district Head's Decree.
5. Establishment of Urban Village/Village FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be stipulated by the Urban Village Head/Village Head's decree.
6. Further provisions regarding organizational structure and FPKK elements shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

The duties and functions of FPKK as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (1) are:

a. coordinating and synchronizing prevention, services, and empowerment for victims of violence against women and children,

b. maintaining and developing FPKK in prevention, services, and empowerment of victims of violence through networking and referral systems,

c. conducting education on non-discrimination values toward women and children,

d. socializing laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence,

e. collecting, compiling, and presenting reports on data of victims of violence, and

f. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 39

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. forming family partners at the urban village/village level by the community,
b. forming women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 40

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of Women and Children in the Region are declared to remain in force as long as they have not been replaced and do not conflict with the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation must be stipulated no later than 6 (six) months from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

Gorontalo.

heading: SECRETARY
translated_text:
SECRETARY

OF

GORONTALO

REGENCY,

ELUCIDATION

OF

GORONTALO REGENCY REGIONAL REGULATION

NUMBER 4. YEAR 2018

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, protection must be provided for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.
